title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: BERNIE'S BRISKET
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight: Bernie Watts, who works at a tire shop in Kansas City, Kansas.
Every summer, her street holds a barbecue contest. Bernie brings store-bought coleslaw.
This year, she brought a smoker. Sort of.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE COLESLAW
segments.quote: The only real stumbling block is fear of failure. In cooking you've got to have a what-the-hell attitude.
segments.author: Julia Child
lines: Her neighbor Duane has won nine years straight. He calls himself the Brisket King.
Bernie said she might enter. Duane laughed. You can't even make toast.
That night, Julia Child was on TV, saying it plain:
The only real stumbling block is fear of failure. In cooking you've got to have a what-the-hell attitude.
Next day, Bernie bought a forty-dollar smoker at a yard sale. It came with a free spider.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE FIRE TRUCK
segments.quote: Wisdom is the daughter of experience.
segments.author: Leonardo da Vinci
lines: Her first brisket came out black as a tire. A fire truck came. Duane waved.
Across the street lived Otis, eighty-two, a pitmaster for forty years.
Bernie remembered a line from Leonardo da Vinci:
Wisdom is the daughter of experience.
So she knocked on Otis's door with a pound cake and asked him to teach her.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: LOW AND SLOW
segments.quote: Governing a great nation is like cooking a small fish - too much handling will spoil it.
segments.author: Lao Tzu
lines: Otis agreed, for more pound cake. Rule one: stop opening the lid.
Bernie opened it every ten minutes. Just to say hi.
Otis quoted Lao Tzu:
Governing a great nation is like cooking a small fish - too much handling will spoil it.
Bernie said, I'm not governing anything. Otis said, Exactly. Close the lid.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE STORM
segments.quote: Victory belongs to the most persevering.
segments.author: Napoleon Bonaparte
lines: Contest night, a storm hit at three a.m. Bernie's fire went out.
She stood there soaked, ready to go back to coleslaw.
Then she saw her late dad's garage sign, a line from Napoleon:
Victory belongs to the most persevering.
So she relit it under a beach umbrella and guarded it till sunrise.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE KING'S FIRE
segments.quote: A candle loses nothing by lighting another candle.
segments.author: James Keller
lines: At sunrise she heard yelling. Duane's fire was out too.
Bernie could win by doing nothing.
But Otis sipped his coffee and quoted the writer James Keller:
A candle loses nothing by lighting another candle.
So Bernie carried hot coals across the street. Duane said thank you. First time ever.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: ONE LONG TABLE
segments.quote: Food is our common ground, a universal experience.
segments.author: James Beard
lines: Duane's brisket won. Bernie's came second, by one point.
Then the whole street sat at one long table, and Otis quoted the chef James Beard:
Food is our common ground, a universal experience.
Now Bernie and Duane smoke the briskets together. Bernie still brings coleslaw. Homemade.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Try it. Ask for help. Be patient. Hang on. Share your fire. Pull up a chair.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Try it anyway. Ask for help. Keep the lid closed. Hang on. Share your fire.
Me? I once smoked a brisket so long, it qualified for Social Security.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
